title: Regular fibres of the map between extended fibres of a tower
statement: Let A → B → C be a tower of commutative rings with compatible algebra structures, and assume B → C is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. For a prime p of A [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and a finite field extension K/κ(p), put D=K⊗[κ(p)](p.Fiber B) and E=K⊗[κ(p)](p.Fiber C). Give E its D-algebra structure by tensoring B → C with the two identity maps. Then for every prime q of D the fibre q.Fiber E is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. No regularity of A → B, no Noetherianity of p.Fiber C, and no purely inseparable hypothesis on K are assumed.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07QI (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07QI), the base-change reduction; Algebra Lemma 0381 (https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0381).

proof.text: First prove the generic base-change fibre statement. If R → S is regular and R → R′ is essentially of finite type, then for q in Spec R′ put p=q∩R and install the canonical residue-field algebra via Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver. The Mathlib generalization recorded by the residue-field finite-generation node gives Algebra.EssFiniteType κ(p) κ(q), hence the extension is finitely generated as a field. Geometric regularity of p.Fiber S and 0381 give regularity of κ(q)⊗[κ(p)](p.Fiber S). Two cancelBaseChange equivalences identify this with q.Fiber (R′⊗[R]S). Transport regularity through those ring equivalences.

For the tower put X=κ(p)⊗[A]B, Y=κ(p)⊗[A]C, D=K⊗[κ(p)]X, E=K⊗[κ(p)]Y. The residue field is essentially finite type over A, so tensor symmetry and essential finite-type base change make B → X essentially finite type. Likewise K is module-finite over κ(p), so X → D is essentially finite type. Compose to get B → D essentially finite type.

Use the pushout cancelBaseChangeAlg equivalences Y ≅ X⊗[B]C and E ≅ D⊗[X]Y, extend the first over D, and cancel X to obtain a D-algebra equivalence E ≅ D⊗[B]C. The commutation with D is verified by cancelBaseChange_symm_comp_lTensor. Apply the generic fibre assertion from step 1 to B → C and B → D, then tensor the D-algebra equivalence with κ(q) to obtain regularity of q.Fiber E. This is a fully proved transport, with no extra hypotheses; the zero rings are covered by the same equivalences.
